capital-accumulation-equation.name: Capital Accumulation Equation
capital-accumulation-equation.title: Capital Accumulation Equation
capital-accumulation-equation.summary: K_{t+1} = I_t + (1 − δ)K_t: next period's capital is new investment plus undepreciated capital; with I = sY it becomes the law of motion that drives growth models.

ces-production-function.name: CES Production Function
ces-production-function.title: CES Production Function
ces-production-function.summary: A production function with a constant elasticity of substitution σ between inputs, nesting perfect substitutes, Cobb-Douglas and Leontief.

change-of-variables.name: Change of Variables
change-of-variables.title: Change of Variables
change-of-variables.summary: Substituting x = g⁻¹(y) rescales integrals by |dx/dy| (the Jacobian determinant in many dimensions); for densities f_Y(y) = f_X(g⁻¹(y))·|dg⁻¹/dy|, e.g. if ln W ~ N(μ, σ²) then E[W] = e^(μ + σ²/2).

classical-measurement-error.name: Classical Measurement Error
classical-measurement-error.title: Classical Measurement Error
classical-measurement-error.summary: Observed = true + independent noise: means stay unbiased because noise averages out, but variances are inflated by the noise variance and OLS slopes on a mismeasured regressor shrink toward zero.

clustered-standard-errors.name: Clustered Standard Errors
clustered-standard-errors.title: Clustered Standard Errors
clustered-standard-errors.summary: When errors are correlated within groups (states, industries, firms), conventional standard errors are too small; cluster-robust standard errors allow any correlation within clusters — roughly a √(1+(m−1)ρ_xρ_e) inflation.

cobb-douglas-production-function.name: Cobb-Douglas Production Function
cobb-douglas-production-function.title: Cobb-Douglas Production Function
cobb-douglas-production-function.summary: Y = AK^α L^(1−α): constant returns, factor shares fixed at α and 1−α, MPK = αY/K diminishing in K, unit elasticity of substitution; any technology term can be rewritten as labor-augmenting.

coefficient-of-determination.name: Coefficient of Determination
coefficient-of-determination.title: Coefficient of Determination
coefficient-of-determination.summary: R² = ESS/TSS = 1 − SSR/TSS: the share of the sample variation of y around its mean that the fitted values account for. It measures fit, not causality or correctness, and compares only models with the same y.

coefficient-of-variation.name: Coefficient of Variation
coefficient-of-variation.title: Coefficient of Variation
coefficient-of-variation.summary: Standard deviation divided by the mean: a scale-invariant dispersion measure dominated by the top of the distribution.

college-wage-bill-share-1967-2017.name: College Wage Bill Share 1967-2017
college-wage-bill-share-1967-2017.title: College Wage Bill Share 1967-2017
college-wage-bill-share-1967-2017.summary: The college share of the US wage bill rose from ≈20% (1967) to 54.7% (2017); 33.6 of the 34.7 pp came from within industries.

column-space.name: Column Space
column-space.title: Column Space
column-space.summary: The column space of A is the set of all linear combinations of its columns; Ax = b has a solution iff b lies in it, and OLS fitted values are the closest point in col(X) to y.

commuting-zone.name: Commuting Zone
commuting-zone.title: Commuting Zone
commuting-zone.summary: A cluster of counties tied together by strong commuting flows, used as the local labor market; 722 CZs cover the whole mainland US, rural areas included, and are the standard unit for regional labor analysis.

composition-adjustment.name: Composition Adjustment
composition-adjustment.title: Composition Adjustment
composition-adjustment.summary: Averaging with sub-group weights held fixed over time, so a group's average wage tracks prices rather than changes in who is in the group; applied to a variance, it separates composition shifts from changes within groups.

conditional-mean-vs-linear-projection.name: Conditional Mean vs Linear Projection
conditional-mean-vs-linear-projection.title: Conditional Mean vs Linear Projection
conditional-mean-vs-linear-projection.summary: E[y|x] is the best predictor and can take any shape; the linear projection α+βx is the best linear predictor and always exists. They coincide only if E[y|x] is linear.

confidence-vs-prediction-intervals.name: Confidence vs Prediction Intervals
confidence-vs-prediction-intervals.title: Confidence vs Prediction Intervals
confidence-vs-prediction-intervals.summary: A confidence interval covers the mean response E[y|x₀]; a prediction interval also covers a new observation's own error, so it is wider and never shrinks to zero.

constrained-optimization-and-lagrange-mu.name: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multipliers
constrained-optimization-and-lagrange-mu.title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multipliers
constrained-optimization-and-lagrange-mu.summary: To optimize f(x) subject to g(x) = c, set up L = f + λ(c − g) and solve ∇L = 0; at the optimum ∇f is parallel to ∇g, and λ is the shadow value of relaxing the constraint by one unit.

consumption-euler-equation.name: Consumption Euler Equation
consumption-euler-equation.title: Consumption Euler Equation
consumption-euler-equation.summary: Optimal saving sets the MRS between today and tomorrow equal to the gross return: u′(c₁) = β(1+r)u′(c₂). With log utility, c₂ = β(1+r)c₁; with capital, the MPK replaces the interest rate.

convexity-and-concavity.summary: f is concave if the chord lies below the graph (Hessian NSD), convex if above (Hessian PSD); concavity makes critical points global maxima, and Jensen's inequality gives E[ln W] ≤ ln E[W].

econ-424-l2-between-group-inequality.summary: The US college premium rose despite rising relative skill supply, so demand grew faster; the canonical CES model with a demand trend fits 1963–2017 with σ ≈ 2.3.

objectives.md: Compute composition-adjusted and unadjusted premia from a small table, and explain the difference.
Use a supply-demand diagram to argue that relative demand must have risen.
Derive the relative wage equation from the CES production function.
Explain why skill-augmenting technology raises the premium only if $\sigma > 1$.
State the identifying assumption of the canonical model, and why including a trend changes it.
Recover $\sigma$ from $\hat\beta$, and convert the trend into relative demand growth.
Compute a shift-share decomposition and give two reasons not to read it causally.

econ-424-l3-total-and-within-group-inequ.name: Econ 424 L3 Total and Within-Group Inequality

econ-424-l3-total-and-within-group-inequ.path: Courses/Econ 424/Lectures/Econ 424 L3 Total and Within-Group Inequality.md
econ-424-l3-total-and-within-group-inequ.summary: US wage inequality rose everywhere in the 1980s; after that, within-group inequality fell for less-educated workers and rose for college graduates, much of the later rise is composition, and the overall pattern is wage polarization.

objectives.md: Derive the college premium $\kappa$ in the unobserved-ability model and show $d\kappa/d\zeta > 0$; explain why within-group inequality rises too.
Compute total, within and between variance of log wages from a small grouped table.
Explain why May/MORG data are better than the March CPS for wage *dispersion* but give similar *averages*.
Explain how top coding biases the variance and hides changes at the top, and name data that avoid it.
Compute a composition-adjusted variance and interpret "2001 equals 1979".
Describe the timing: a pervasive rise in the 1980s, then falling within-group inequality for the less educated and rising for college graduates.
Define wage polarization using the 90-50 and 50-10 gaps and read a growth-by-percentile chart.
Explain why the "within share" depends on how finely groups are defined.

econ-424-l4-international-trade-theory.name: Econ 424 L4 International Trade Theory
econ-424-l4-international-trade-theory.title: International trade theory
econ-424-l4-international-trade-theory.summary: Trade changes world demand for domestic goods, hence their prices; with immobile factors each factor's income moves with its goods' prices, so a region or factor gains by its income-share-weighted exposure, d log w_r = Σ_j λ_rj d log p_j.

objectives.md: Explain, in words, how trade liberalization changes relative wages across industries, firms and regions, and why mobility undoes it.
Show that with immobile factors and constant factor shares, $d\log(\text{factor payments}_j) = d\log p_j$.
Derive $d\log w_r = \sum_j \lambda_{rj}\,d\log p_j$ from $w_r = \sum_j s_{rj}w_j$, and explain why the weights are income shares.
Compute regional or factor wage changes from shares and price changes, and the relative change between two regions.
Say which regions or factors gain from export and import shocks.

kovak-2013-regional-effects-of-trade-ref.path: Papers/Kovak 2013 - Regional Effects of Trade Reform.md
kovak-2013-regional-effects-of-trade-ref.summary: A specific-factors model implies the right regional liberalization measure weights tariff cuts by traded-industry labor shares and excludes non-traded sectors; in Brazil, regions facing 10% larger cuts saw ≈4.4% larger wage declines.

law-of-iterated-expectations.name: Law of Iterated Expectations
law-of-iterated-expectations.title: Law of Iterated Expectations
law-of-iterated-expectations.summary: E[E[Y|X]] = E[Y]: the overall average is the probability-weighted average of the conditional averages.

law-of-total-variance.name: Law of Total Variance
law-of-total-variance.title: Law of Total Variance
law-of-total-variance.summary: Var(Y) = E[Var(Y|X)] + Var(E[Y|X]): total variance is average within-group variance plus the variance of group means.

leibniz-integral-rule.name: Leibniz Integral Rule
leibniz-integral-rule.title: Leibniz Integral Rule
leibniz-integral-rule.summary: d/dt ∫_{a(t)}^{b(t)} f(x,t)dx = f(b,t)b′ − f(a,t)a′ + ∫ ∂f/∂t dx; it differentiates expected values with respect to choice variables, e.g. the newsvendor optimum F(q*) = (p − c)/p.

lemieux-2006-increasing-residual-wage-in.name: Lemieux 2006 - Increasing Residual Wage Inequality
lemieux-2006-increasing-residual-wage-in.title: Increasing Residual Wage Inequality: Composition Effects, Noisy Data, or Rising Demand for Skill?
lemieux-2006-increasing-residual-wage-in.summary: Much of the post-1980s rise in US within-group (residual) wage inequality is a composition effect from an older, more educated workforce, plus noise in March CPS wages; the genuine rise is concentrated in the 1980s.

assets/Attachments/US within-education variance of log wages 1973-2009.png

lhopitals-rule.name: L'Hôpital's Rule
lhopitals-rule.title: L'Hôpital's Rule
lhopitals-rule.summary: For a 0/0 or ∞/∞ limit, lim f/g = lim f'/g'; it shows the Box-Cox transform tends to ln x as λ → 0 and the CES production function tends to Cobb-Douglas as σ → 1.

linear-independence-and-rank.name: Linear Independence and Rank
linear-independence-and-rank.title: Linear Independence and Rank
linear-independence-and-rank.summary: Vectors are linearly independent if none is a combination of the others; rank = number of independent columns, rank + nullity = number of columns, and rank(X'X) = rank(X).

log-change-taylor-expansion.name: Log Change Taylor Expansion
log-change-taylor-expansion.title: Log Change Taylor Expansion
log-change-taylor-expansion.summary: ln(1 + x) expanded around a = 0 as one shared model - the exact log change, its first-order approximation x, its second-order approximation x - x²/2, and the error of each.

log-wage-gap.name: Log Wage Gap
log-wage-gap.title: Log Wage Gap
log-wage-gap.summary: The difference in log average wages between two groups — the standard scale-invariant measure of between-group inequality.

logarithms-and-growth-rates.name: Logarithms and Growth Rates
logarithms-and-growth-rates.title: Logarithms and Growth Rates
logarithms-and-growth-rates.summary: d ln y = dy/y: log changes are proportional changes, log differences ≈ percentage changes (exactly e^Δ − 1), they add over time and are symmetric, and elasticities are d ln y / d ln x.

lognormal-inequality-explorer.name: Lognormal Inequality Explorer
lognormal-inequality-explorer.title: Lognormal Inequality Explorer
lognormal-inequality-explorer.summary: Wages drawn from a lognormal. Drag σ, the spread of log wages, and watch the Lorenz curve bow and the Gini, percentile ratios, variance of logs and top 10% share move together. Drag μ and none of them change.

longitudinal-business-database-lbd.name: Longitudinal Business Database (LBD)
longitudinal-business-database-lbd.title: Longitudinal Business Database (LBD)
longitudinal-business-database-lbd.summary: US Census Bureau panel tracking employment, payroll and industry of virtually every establishment with employees in the nonfarm private economy, annually; restricted access.

lorenz-curve.name: Lorenz Curve
lorenz-curve.title: Lorenz Curve
lorenz-curve.summary: The share of total income held by the bottom x% of the population, for every x — a full picture of a distribution, not a single-number measure.

lowess-smoother.name: Lowess Smoother
lowess-smoother.title: Lowess Smoother
lowess-smoother.summary: Lowess fits a weighted least-squares line in a moving window around each x and joins the fitted values, tracing E[y|x] without assuming a shape; divergence from the OLS line flags nonlinearity.
figures: assets/Attachments/Scatterplot with OLS line and lowess - prestige on income.png
assets/Attachments/Vocabulary on education - jittered with OLS line and lowess.png

marginal-rate-of-substitution.name: Marginal Rate of Substitution
marginal-rate-of-substitution.title: Marginal Rate of Substitution
marginal-rate-of-substitution.summary: The MRS is the ratio of marginal utilities, U₁/U₂: how much of good 2 you would give up for one more unit of good 1. At an optimum it equals the price ratio; diminishing MRS makes people prefer balanced bundles.
figures: assets/Attachments/Two-period saving model - reading MRS equals 1 plus r.png

market-clearing.name: Market Clearing
market-clearing.title: Market Clearing
market-clearing.summary: Equilibrium requires total demand to equal total supply; in an endowment economy, total consumption equals total income each period, so aggregate saving is zero and the interest rate adjusts until borrowers' demand meets savers' supply.
figures: assets/Attachments/Two-period saving model - market clearing with two consumers.png
assets/Attachments/Two-period saving model - solving for the equilibrium interest rate.png
assets/Attachments/Two-period saving model - income shocks and the interest rate.png
assets/Attachments/Two-period saving model - patience and the interest rate.png

math-prep-l1-matrix-algebra-essentials.name: Math Prep L1 Matrix Algebra Essentials
math-prep-l1-matrix-algebra-essentials.title: Matrix Algebra Essentials
math-prep-l1-matrix-algebra-essentials.path: Courses/Math Prep/Lectures/Math Prep L1 Matrix Algebra Essentials.md
math-prep-l1-matrix-algebra-essentials.summary: The matrix rules every regression derivation uses: order and reversal rules, when an inverse exists, block (partitioned) inverses, and the trace tricks behind degrees of freedom.
math-prep-l1-matrix-algebra-essentials.source: Refresher authored for the vault (no lecture source)

objectives.md: Transpose and invert products without reversing the order wrongly.
State the equivalent conditions for invertibility, and connect them to identification.
Use the partitioned inverse to get the block of $(\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X})^{-1}$ for a subset of regressors.
Use the cyclic trace property to compute $E[\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}'\mathbf{M}\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}]$.

math-prep-l2-vector-spaces-rank-and-proj.name: Math Prep L2 Vector Spaces Rank and Projection
math-prep-l2-vector-spaces-rank-and-proj.title: Vector Spaces, Rank and Projection
math-prep-l2-vector-spaces-rank-and-proj.path: Courses/Math Prep/Lectures/Math Prep L2 Vector Spaces Rank and Projection.md
math-prep-l2-vector-spaces-rank-and-proj.summary: Least squares is geometry: fitted values live in the column space of X, full rank makes the coefficients unique, and OLS is the orthogonal projection of y onto col(X), leaving residuals orthogonal to every regressor.
math-prep-l2-vector-spaces-rank-and-proj.source: Refresher authored for the vault (no lecture source)

objectives.md: Read $\mathbf{X}\mathbf{b}$ as a linear combination of columns.
Find the rank of a design matrix and spot exact linear dependence.
Explain the normal equations as an orthogonality condition.
Compute a projection onto a vector and onto a column space.

math-prep-l3-eigenvalues-and-quadratic-f.name: Math Prep L3 Eigenvalues and Quadratic Forms
math-prep-l3-eigenvalues-and-quadratic-f.title: Eigenvalues and Quadratic Forms
math-prep-l3-eigenvalues-and-quadratic-f.path: Courses/Math Prep/Lectures/Math Prep L3 Eigenvalues and Quadratic Forms.md
math-prep-l3-eigenvalues-and-quadratic-f.summary: Eigenvalues summarise what a matrix does; symmetric matrices diagonalise as QΛQ', and the signs of their eigenvalues decide whether a quadratic form — and so a Hessian or X'X — is positive definite.
math-prep-l3-eigenvalues-and-quadratic-f.source: Refresher authored for the vault (no lecture source)

objectives.md: Compute the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a $2\times2$ symmetric matrix.
Use eigenvalues to read off trace, determinant, rank and invertibility.
Test a matrix for definiteness two ways.
Explain why $\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X}$ is PD exactly under full rank.

math-prep-l4-multivariable-differentiati.name: Math Prep L4 Multivariable Differentiation
math-prep-l4-multivariable-differentiati.title: Multivariable Differentiation
math-prep-l4-multivariable-differentiati.path: Courses/Math Prep/Lectures/Math Prep L4 Multivariable Differentiation.md
math-prep-l4-multivariable-differentiati.summary: Partials are ceteris-paribus marginal effects; the chain rule, Hessian and implicit function theorem handle co-movement, curvature and comparative statics; homogeneity makes relative wages depend only on relative supply.
math-prep-l4-multivariable-differentiati.source: Refresher authored for the vault (no lecture source)

objectives.md: Compute partials and a gradient, and interpret them as marginal effects.
Distinguish partial from total derivatives; do growth accounting.
Build a Hessian and classify a critical point.
Do comparative statics with the implicit function theorem.
Use Euler's theorem to show factor payments exhaust output under CRS.

math-prep-l5-matrix-calculus.name: Math Prep L5 Matrix Calculus
math-prep-l5-matrix-calculus.title: Matrix Calculus
math-prep-l5-matrix-calculus.path: Courses/Math Prep/Lectures/Math Prep L5 Matrix Calculus.md
math-prep-l5-matrix-calculus.summary: Two rules — ∂(a'x)/∂x = a and ∂(x'Ax)/∂x = (A + A')x — are enough to derive the OLS normal equations, their solution and the second-order condition in four lines.
math-prep-l5-matrix-calculus.source: Refresher authored for the vault (no lecture source)

objectives.md: Differentiate linear and quadratic forms with respect to a vector.
Derive the OLS normal equations and solution from scratch.
State and verify the second-order condition.
Check every derivative's dimensions.

math-prep-l6-optimization.name: Math Prep L6 Optimization
math-prep-l6-optimization.title: Optimization
math-prep-l6-optimization.summary: Interior optima satisfy ∇f = 0 with a definite Hessian; concavity makes them global; constraints add a Lagrange multiplier that prices the constraint; and the envelope theorem gives value-function derivatives for free.
math-prep-l6-optimization.source: Refresher authored for the vault (no lecture source)

objectives.md: Solve unconstrained problems and verify the second-order condition.
Use concavity to argue a critical point is a global optimum.
Set up and solve a Lagrangian, and interpret the multiplier.
Apply the envelope theorem to get value-function derivatives.
State Jensen's inequality and apply it to logs.

math-prep-l7-approximations-logs-and-ser.name: Math Prep L7 Approximations Logs and Series
math-prep-l7-approximations-logs-and-ser.title: Approximations, Logs and Series
math-prep-l7-approximations-logs-and-ser.path: Courses/Math Prep/Lectures/Math Prep L7 Approximations Logs and Series.md
math-prep-l7-approximations-logs-and-ser.summary: Taylor expansions justify log approximations and linear models; log differences are proportional changes (exactly e^Δ − 1); L'Hôpital gives the Box-Cox and Cobb-Douglas limits; geometric series price streams and AR processes.
math-prep-l7-approximations-logs-and-ser.source: Refresher authored for the vault (no lecture source)

objectives.md: Write first- and second-order Taylor approximations and judge their accuracy.
Convert between log differences and exact percentage changes.
Interpret an elasticity as a log derivative.
Evaluate $0/0$ limits with L'Hôpital, including the Box-Cox and CES limits.
Price annuities and perpetuities, and compute an AR(1) variance.

math-prep-l8-integration-for-probability.name: Math Prep L8 Integration for Probability
math-prep-l8-integration-for-probability.title: Integration for Probability and Economics
math-prep-l8-integration-for-probability.path: Courses/Math Prep/Lectures/Math Prep L8 Integration for Probability.md
math-prep-l8-integration-for-probability.summary: The integration you actually need in economics is for expectations: integration by parts (E[X] = ∫(1 − F)), change of variables (lognormal wages), Leibniz's rule (differentiating expected values) and double integrals (joint densities, LIE).
math-prep-l8-integration-for-probability.source: Refresher authored for the vault (no lecture source)

objectives.md: Compute expectations by parts, including via the survival function.
Derive the density of a transformed variable; know the lognormal mean.
Differentiate an integral whose limits depend on a choice variable.
Get marginal densities and expectations from a joint density; prove the LIE for continuous variables.

matrix-algebra-identities.name: Matrix Algebra Identities
matrix-algebra-identities.title: Matrix Algebra Identities
matrix-algebra-identities.summary: Core matrix rules: multiplication is associative but not commutative, (AB)' = B'A', (AB)⁻¹ = B⁻¹A⁻¹ and (A')⁻¹ = (A⁻¹)' — the reversal rules behind every regression derivation.

matrix-calculus.name: Matrix Calculus
matrix-calculus.title: Matrix Calculus
matrix-calculus.summary: Rules for differentiating scalars with respect to vectors: ∂(a'x)/∂x = a, ∂(x'Ax)/∂x = (A + A')x (= 2Ax if A is symmetric); with them, ∂(e'e)/∂b = −2X'(y − Xb) gives the OLS normal equations.

multivariable-chain-rule.name: Multivariable Chain Rule
multivariable-chain-rule.title: Multivariable Chain Rule
multivariable-chain-rule.summary: When inputs themselves depend on t, df/dt = Σ (∂f/∂xᵢ)(dxᵢ/dt); the total differential df = Σ fᵢ dxᵢ and, in logs, growth accounting g_Y = g_A + α g_K + (1−α) g_L.

ols-estimator.name: OLS Estimator
ols-estimator.title: OLS Estimator
ols-estimator.summary: Least-squares estimates b₂ = Σ(x−x̄)(y−ȳ)/Σ(x−x̄)² and b₁ = ȳ − b₂x̄ from the normal equations; unbiased under linearity, exogeneity and variation in x, without homoskedasticity.
figures: assets/Attachments/Food expenditure regression - fitted line.png

ols-in-matrix-form.name: OLS in Matrix Form
ols-in-matrix-form.title: OLS in Matrix Form
ols-in-matrix-form.summary: b = (X'X)⁻¹X'y from minimising e'e, with residuals orthogonal to every regressor (X'e = 0).

ols-line-fitter.name: OLS Line Fitter
ols-line-fitter.title: OLS Line Fitter
ols-line-fitter.summary: Fit a line to forty simulated households by hand: drag the intercept b₁ and slope b₂, watch the squared residuals and SSR shrink, then reveal the least-squares line.

ols-sampling-distribution.name: OLS Sampling Distribution
ols-sampling-distribution.title: OLS Sampling Distribution
ols-sampling-distribution.summary: Histogram the OLS slope b₂ over up to 2,000 samples: it centres on β₂ with the spread its standard error predicts; heteroskedasticity breaks the textbook SE, x correlated with the error moves the centre.

ols-sampling-model.name: OLS Sampling Model
ols-sampling-model.title: OLS Sampling Model
ols-sampling-model.summary: The food-expenditure population for repeated sampling: y = β₁ + β₂x + γz + e with N households, error spread σ (optionally growing with income), an error that can move with x (SR2 fails), and R samples.

partial-derivatives-and-the-gradient.name: Partial Derivatives and the Gradient
partial-derivatives-and-the-gradient.title: Partial Derivatives and the Gradient
partial-derivatives-and-the-gradient.summary: A partial derivative ∂f/∂xᵢ changes one input holding the others fixed; stacking them gives the gradient ∇f, which points in the direction of steepest ascent and is zero at an interior optimum.

partitioned-matrices.name: Partitioned Matrices
partitioned-matrices.title: Partitioned Matrices
partitioned-matrices.summary: Block matrices multiply like scalars (respecting order), and the partitioned inverse gives the lower-right block of (X'X)⁻¹ as (X₂'M₁X₂)⁻¹ — the algebra behind Frisch–Waugh–Lovell.

percentile-ratios.name: Percentile Ratios
percentile-ratios.title: Percentile Ratios
percentile-ratios.summary: Log gaps between percentiles such as 90-10, 90-50 and 50-10; they add up, separating upper-tail from lower-tail inequality.

pierce-and-schott-2016-the-surprisingly-.name: Pierce and Schott 2016 - The Surprisingly Swift Decline of US Manufacturing Employment
pierce-and-schott-2016-the-surprisingly-.title: The Surprisingly Swift Decline of US Manufacturing Employment
pierce-and-schott-2016-the-surprisingly-.path: Papers/Pierce and Schott 2016 - The Surprisingly Swift Decline of US Manufacturing Employment.md
pierce-and-schott-2016-the-surprisingly-.summary: Granting China permanent normal trade relations in 2001 removed the threat of tariff spikes; US industries with larger NTR gaps lost more employment afterwards (25th→75th gap ≈ −8 log points), with losses growing over time.

projection-matrix-and-residual-maker.name: Projection Matrix and Residual Maker
projection-matrix-and-residual-maker.title: Projection Matrix and Residual Maker
projection-matrix-and-residual-maker.summary: P = X(X'X)⁻¹X' projects y onto the column space of X and M = I − P produces the residuals; both are symmetric and idempotent, and MX = 0.

properties-of-inequality-measures.name: Properties of Inequality Measures
properties-of-inequality-measures.title: Properties of Inequality Measures
properties-of-inequality-measures.summary: Scale invariance, the transfer principle, decomposability and tail sensitivity — the criteria for comparing inequality measures — plus Lorenz dominance.

q-q-plot.name: Q-Q Plot
q-q-plot.title: Q-Q Plot
q-q-plot.summary: A Q-Q plot graphs sample quantiles against a reference distribution's quantiles: a straight line means the reference fits; a convex bend means right skew, and ends bending away in opposite directions mean heavy tails.
figures: assets/Attachments/QQ plot - Prestige income.png
assets/Attachments/QQ plots - Prestige income by occupation type.png
assets/Attachments/QQ plot - standardized residuals of the prestige regression.png

quadratic-form-explorer.name: Quadratic Form Explorer
quadratic-form-explorer.title: Quadratic Form Explorer
quadratic-form-explorer.summary: Move the entries of a 2×2 symmetric matrix and see from the level sets of x′Ax, its eigenvectors and the signs of its eigenvalues whether it is definite, semidefinite or indefinite.

quadratic-forms-and-definiteness.name: Quadratic Forms and Definiteness
quadratic-forms-and-definiteness.title: Quadratic Forms and Definiteness
quadratic-forms-and-definiteness.summary: A quadratic form x'Ax is positive definite if it is > 0 for every x ≠ 0 — iff all eigenvalues (or leading principal minors) are positive; X'X is always PSD and PD under full rank.

regression-diagnostics.name: Regression Diagnostics
regression-diagnostics.title: Regression Diagnostics
regression-diagnostics.summary: Residual, QQ and leverage plots that detect nonlinearity, heteroskedasticity, non-normality and influential observations after fitting OLS.

relative-supply-and-demand.name: Relative Supply and Demand
relative-supply-and-demand.title: Relative Supply and Demand
relative-supply-and-demand.summary: The relative wage of two groups is set where relative demand meets relative supply; rising supply with a rising price implies demand grew faster.

sampling-distribution-of-ols.name: Sampling Distribution of OLS
sampling-distribution-of-ols.title: Sampling Distribution of OLS
sampling-distribution-of-ols.summary: OLS estimators are (approximately) normal around β; with σ² estimated by RSS/(N−2), t = (b−β)/se(b) follows a t distribution with N−2 df.

saving-investment-identity.name: Saving-Investment Identity
saving-investment-identity.title: Saving-Investment Identity
saving-investment-identity.summary: In a closed economy with no government, Y = C + I and S = Y − C, so saving equals investment (S = I); with a fixed saving rate, investment is sY.

shift-share-decomposition.name: Shift-Share Decomposition
shift-share-decomposition.title: Shift-Share Decomposition
shift-share-decomposition.summary: An exact accounting split of a change in an aggregate share into between-unit (mix) and within-unit (intensity) parts — descriptive, not causal.

shift-share-exposure.name: Shift-Share Exposure
shift-share-exposure.title: Shift-Share Exposure
shift-share-exposure.summary: A unit's exposure to sector-level shocks is its share-weighted average of the shocks, Σ_j λ_rj·shock_j; with immobile factors, d log w_r = Σ_j λ_rj d log p_j exactly to first order.

shift-share-instrument.name: Shift-Share Instrument
shift-share-instrument.title: Shift-Share Instrument
shift-share-instrument.summary: Instrument a unit's exposure with base-period shares times shocks measured elsewhere (e.g. Chinese import growth in other rich countries), so the instrument reflects foreign supply shocks rather than domestic demand shocks.

shift-share-wage-exposure-explorer.name: Shift-Share Wage Exposure Explorer
shift-share-wage-exposure-explorer.title: Shift-Share Wage Exposure Explorer
shift-share-wage-exposure-explorer.summary: Drag two regions along the exposure line and move the two goods' price changes to see that a region's wage change is an income-share-weighted average of price changes, and that only relative price changes redistribute.

simple-linear-regression-model.name: Simple Linear Regression Model
simple-linear-regression-model.title: Simple Linear Regression Model
simple-linear-regression-model.summary: y = β₁ + β₂x + e: a model of the conditional mean of y given x, with e collecting everything else.
figures: assets/Attachments/Food expenditure and income - histograms and conditional distributions.png

skewness-and-kurtosis.name: Skewness and Kurtosis
skewness-and-kurtosis.title: Skewness and Kurtosis
skewness-and-kurtosis.summary: Skewness S = E[(X−μ)³]/σ³ measures lopsidedness (0 if symmetric); kurtosis K = E[(X−μ)⁴]/σ⁴ measures tail weight (3 for a normal). Software often reports excess kurtosis K − 3.

skill-premium.name: Skill Premium
skill-premium.title: Skill Premium
skill-premium.summary: The composition-adjusted log wage gap between college and non-college workers — the price of skill.

small-open-economy.name: Small Open Economy
small-open-economy.title: Small Open Economy
small-open-economy.summary: An economy too small to affect world prices, so it takes the prices of traded goods (and often the interest rate) as given; trade shocks reach it as exogenous price changes.

solow-convergence-and-shocks.name: Solow Convergence and Shocks
solow-convergence-and-shocks.title: Solow Convergence and Shocks
solow-convergence-and-shocks.summary: Iterate the per-worker law of motion from any starting capital and watch k converge to k̄, quickly at first; then change s or δ at date t* and follow capital, output and consumption to the new steady state.

solow-diagram.name: Solow Diagram
solow-diagram.title: Solow Diagram
solow-diagram.summary: Plot investment sf(k) and depreciation δk against capital per worker: the gap is Δk, the crossing is the steady state, and shifting the curve (s, A) or rotating the line (δ) shows every shock's long-run effect and transition.
figures: assets/Attachments/Solow diagram - investment vs depreciation.png
assets/Attachments/Solow diagram - rise in depreciation.png

assets/Attachments/Solow diagram - rise in population growth with technological progress.png

solow-golden-rule-explorer.name: Solow Golden Rule Explorer
solow-golden-rule-explorer.title: Solow Golden Rule Explorer
solow-golden-rule-explorer.summary: Move the saving rate and watch steady-state consumption, the gap between f(k̄) and δk̄, grow and then shrink; it is largest where the slope of f equals δ, which with Cobb-Douglas means s = α.

solow-growth-model.name: Solow Growth Model
solow-growth-model.title: Solow Growth Model
solow-growth-model.summary: Fixed saving, diminishing returns and depreciation drive capital per worker to a steady state k̄ = (sA/δ)^(1/(1−α)) where investment just replaces worn-out capital; saving raises levels, not long-run growth.
figures: assets/Attachments/Solow transition path - capital converging to steady state.png

solow-level-and-growth-effects.name: Solow Level and Growth Effects
solow-level-and-growth-effects.title: Solow Level and Growth Effects
solow-level-and-growth-effects.summary: Capital per effective worker, ln k̃ + ln Ã = ln k, and growth rates over time: raise η at t* for a level effect (a parallel but lower path for ln k) or lower γ for a growth effect (a flatter path).

solow-model-per-effective-worker.name: Solow Model Per Effective Worker
solow-model-per-effective-worker.title: Solow Model Per Effective Worker
solow-model-per-effective-worker.summary: The Solow model with population growth η and technological progress γ, per effective worker - the stationarized law of motion and the balanced-growth steady state that the level-and-growth-effects explorer is a view of.

solow-model-per-worker.name: Solow Model Per Worker
solow-model-per-worker.title: Solow Model Per Worker
solow-model-per-worker.summary: The basic Solow model per worker as one shared model - parameters s, A, α and δ, the law of motion for capital per worker, and the steady-state and golden-rule values that the Solow explorers are views of.

solow-model-with-technological-progress.name: Solow Model with Technological Progress
solow-model-with-technological-progress.title: Solow Model with Technological Progress
solow-model-with-technological-progress.summary: With labor growing at η and TFP at γ, divide by effective labor ÃL: capital per effective worker converges to k̄ = (s/(δ+η+γ̃))^(1/(1−α)), and output per worker then grows at γ̃ = γ/(1−α) forever.

assets/Attachments/Log growth paths - rise in population growth, aggregate capital.png
assets/Attachments/Solow diagram - fall in technology growth with log growth paths.png

solow-steady-state-explorer.name: Solow Steady State Explorer
solow-steady-state-explorer.title: Solow Steady State Explorer
solow-steady-state-explorer.summary: Drag capital per worker along the Solow diagram to see investment minus depreciation, then move s, A, α and δ to see where the curve meets the line and how k̄, ȳ and c̄ respond.

song-et-al-2019-firming-up-inequality.name: Song et al 2019 - Firming Up Inequality
song-et-al-2019-firming-up-inequality.title: Firming Up Inequality
song-et-al-2019-firming-up-inequality.path: Papers/Song et al 2019 - Firming Up Inequality.md
song-et-al-2019-firming-up-inequality.summary: Uncapped Social Security records for all US workers and firms show earnings growth rising steeply with the percentile since the 1980s; most of the rise in inequality is between firms, driven by worker sorting and segregation.
figures: assets/Attachments/US earnings growth by percentile SSA 1982-2012.png

specific-factors-model.name: Specific-Factors Model
specific-factors-model.title: Specific-Factors Model
specific-factors-model.summary: With factors stuck in their industries and output fixed, each factor's income moves one-for-one with its industry's price: d log (factor payments)_j = d log p_j. Winners are factors tied to goods whose prices rise.

spectral-decomposition.name: Spectral Decomposition
spectral-decomposition.title: Spectral Decomposition
spectral-decomposition.summary: Every symmetric matrix factors as A = QΛQ' with orthonormal eigenvectors Q and real eigenvalues Λ, which makes powers, inverses and square roots (A^{-1/2}) easy to compute.

sr-assumptions.name: SR Assumptions
sr-assumptions.title: SR Assumptions
sr-assumptions.summary: The six simple-regression assumptions and what each delivers: unbiasedness needs linearity, exogeneity and variation in x, BLUE needs homoskedasticity, exact inference needs normality.

ssa-master-earnings-file.name: SSA Master Earnings File
ssa-master-earnings-file.title: SSA Master Earnings File
ssa-master-earnings-file.summary: US Social Security Administration records of W-2 earnings for essentially every wage earner, with no top coding — the source for uncapped earnings inequality since the late 1970s, including the top 1%.

steady-state.name: Steady State
steady-state.title: Steady State
steady-state.summary: A steady state is a fixed point of a law of motion, x* = g(x*); it is stable if the economy converges back to it after a shock, which for x_{t+1} = g(x_t) requires |g′(x*)| < 1.

strict-exogeneity.name: Strict Exogeneity
strict-exogeneity.title: Strict Exogeneity
strict-exogeneity.summary: E[e|x] = 0: the regressor carries no information about the error. The only assumption whose failure biases OLS.

taylor-approximation-of-log-change.name: Taylor Approximation of Log Change
taylor-approximation-of-log-change.title: Taylor Approximation of Log Change
taylor-approximation-of-log-change.summary: Move the percentage change x away from zero and watch the first-order line and second-order parabola drift from ln(1 + x); the gap between the line and the log grows fast beyond a few percent.

taylor-series-approximation.name: Taylor Series Approximation
taylor-series-approximation.title: Taylor Series Approximation
taylor-series-approximation.summary: f(x) ≈ f(a) + f'(a)(x − a) + ½f''(a)(x − a)²; the multivariate version uses the gradient and Hessian. It justifies log approximations, second-order conditions and linear models as local approximations.

top-coding.name: Top Coding
top-coding.title: Top Coding
top-coding.summary: Surveys record every income above a cap as the cap itself; this censors the top tail, biases dispersion measures down and makes growth in top incomes invisible.

top-income-shares.name: Top Income Shares
top-income-shares.title: Top Income Shares
top-income-shares.summary: The share of total income received by the top x% (10%, 1%, 0.1%) — one point on the Lorenz curve, best measured with tax data.

trace-of-a-matrix.name: Trace of a Matrix
trace-of-a-matrix.title: Trace of a Matrix
trace-of-a-matrix.summary: trace(A) is the sum of the diagonal; it is linear, cyclic (tr(ABC) = tr(CAB)), equals the sum of eigenvalues, and equals rank for idempotent matrices — the source of N − K degrees of freedom.

two-period-consumer-model.name: Two-Period Consumer Model
two-period-consumer-model.title: Two-Period Consumer Model
two-period-consumer-model.summary: The two-period consumer with log utility U = ln c₁ + β ln c₂ and endowment (y₁, y₂) as one shared model - the lifetime budget line, indifference curves, the optimum where MRS = 1 + r, and saving s = y₁ − c₁.

two-period-consumption-choice.name: Two-Period Consumption Choice
two-period-consumption-choice.title: Two-Period Consumption Choice
two-period-consumption-choice.summary: Drag the endowment and move r and β to see the best bundle where the highest reachable indifference curve touches the lifetime budget line (MRS = 1 + r), and whether it lies left of the endowment (saving) or right of it (borrowing).

two-period-consumption-saving-model.name: Two-Period Consumption-Saving Model
two-period-consumption-saving-model.title: Two-Period Consumption-Saving Model
two-period-consumption-saving-model.summary: Fisher's model: a consumer lives two periods, saves or borrows at rate r to maximize U(c₁, c₂) subject to a lifetime budget; saving reflects consumption smoothing, impatience and the interest rate, and r clears the loan market.

unconstrained-optimization.name: Unconstrained Optimization
unconstrained-optimization.title: Unconstrained Optimization
unconstrained-optimization.summary: Interior optima satisfy the first-order condition ∇f = 0; the second-order condition (Hessian ND for a max, PD for a min) separates maxima, minima and saddles, and concavity makes a local max global.

us-earnings-growth-by-percentile-1982-20.name: US Earnings Growth by Percentile 1982-2012
us-earnings-growth-by-percentile-1982-20.title: US Earnings Growth by Percentile 1982-2012

econ430-l1-kde-bandwidth.description: Precomputed for the Kernel Density Bandwidth Explorer widget in Econ 430 L1, not a data source. n = 1000 draws from an exponential with mean 0.5 (the lecture's x3, replayed from random.seed(10)); true density 2e^(-2x). Tidy long table: a blank h matches every slider value. kde rows hold a Gaussian KDE at each h in [0.01, 0.5] step 0.005 on 300 grid points over [-0.2, 3.5]; ise integrates its squared error against the true density (trapezoid on that grid). econ430-l1-qq-shapes.description: Precomputed for the Q-Q Plot Shape Explorer widget in Econ 430 L1, not a data source; computed with scipy.stats, not from the lecture notebook. n = 100 plotting positions p_i = (i - 0.5)/n; x = Phi^-1(p_i), y = the family's quantile standardized to mean 0 and sd 1 (lognormal by its exact mean and sd, t by sqrt(df/(df-2)), uniform by (u - 1/2) sqrt(12)). df = 2 has infinite variance, so that one position is scaled by IQR/1.349 instead.
